Case: Patient D is a 45-year-old Asian woman with hepatocellular carcinoma status-post C4-C5 corpectomy and fusion 8 months ago who presents with new arm and leg pain. Of note, Patient D endorses unintentional weight loss over the last 2 months which coincided with increased severity of her pain. When describing the pain, she says that she feels intermittent shocks down both arms and legs, and also notes a diffuse ache in her neck and lower back. Physical examination reveals some numbness in her hands and thighs, as well as diffuse spine tenderness. MRI of scans of her entire spine show increased tumor burden in her lumbar and cervical spine causing multiple areas of severe stenosis. You are also able to identify new lesions seeding her peritoneum.
Question: Would you offer morphine to Patient D? Yes or No? If yes, how much supply would you give – Low (1 week), or High (4 weeks) supply? Explain.
